verses.1: He also said to his students: “There was a man who was very rich, and he had a steward who managed his property. This steward misused the wealth that belonged to him.”
verses.2: And he said to him, “What do I hear about you? You’re failing in your duties as a merchant; you can no longer continue to be a merchant.”
verses.3: But the landlord said to himself, “What can I do? Why should my master take away my livelihood from me?” I refuse to do that; I don’t want to ask for such a thing.
verses.4: I don’t know what to do, so that when I leave my current job, you can take me to your own houses.
verses.5: And when he called each of those who owed money to their master, he said to the first one, “How much do you owe my master?”
verses.6: And he said, “One hundred chickens.” But the other person said to him, “Write down the letters for me, and sit down quickly and write fifty of them.”
verses.7: Then he said to the other person, “How much do you owe?” The other person replied, “Eighty children of salt.” He said to him, “Write down the numbers, and write eighty.”
verses.8: And the Lord forgave the steward for his wrongdoing, because he had acted intentionally. He said that the sons of darkness were more righteous than the sons of light, in terms of their own nature.
verses.9: And I say to you, make friends among yourselves from those who have suffered injustice at the hands of others, so that when they are no longer able to support you in these temporal difficulties, they can help you.
verses.10: A person who is trustworthy in the least amount of situations is still trustworthy overall. But a person who is trustworthy only in certain situations is actually not trustworthy at all.
verses.11: If you are not faithful to your mother in this unjust act, then who will truly believe in you?
verses.12: And even if you don’t become believers in that other way, who will give you your due?
verses.13: No householder can serve two masters. For he must either hate one and love the other, or he must despise one and respect the other. It is not possible for a person to serve two lords at the same time.
verses.14: And all these things were heard by the Pharisees, who were greedy for money. They tried to deceive him with these things.
verses.15: And he said to them, “You are those who judge yourselves in the eyes of men. But God will know the hearts of you. For there is a great sin in man’s eyes before God.”
verses.16: The law and the prophets continue until John. From that time on, the kingdom of God is preached, and everyone is tested within it.
verses.17: It is better for heaven and earth to cease existing, rather than for one single rule to be violated.
verses.18: Anyone who divorces his wife and marries another woman commits adultery. And anyone who is divorced from her husband and marries another man also commits adultery.
verses.19: And there was a man who was very rich. He wore pearls and other luxurious items, and he lived a life of comfort and luxury every day.
verses.20: A beggar named Lazarus was laid at his gate, tied up there.
verses.21: And he desired to be freed from those who were around him, from the table of the rich man. But even the dogs that came over, prevented him from getting away.
verses.22: And it happened that the poor man died, and he was taken away by the angels to the tomb of Abraham. The rich man also died, and he was buried there.
verses.23: And in that darkness, Abraham could see from afar his eyes, which were located on his temples. Also, Lazarus could be seen in the valleys surrounding him.
verses.24: And he said, “Father Abraham, have mercy on me. Send Lazarus to wash the tip of my toe with water and to cool my tongue, for I am suffering greatly in this fire.”
verses.25: Abram said, “Son, remember that you received your good things in this life, and Lazar also received his bad things. Now, you must endure this suffering.”
verses.26: And among all these things, a great gap is created between us and you. Thus, those who want to pass from here to you cannot do so, nor can they pass from here to us.
verses.27: He said, “I ask you, father, to send him to my father’s house.”
verses.28: I have five brothers, as it is written in the scriptures, so that they too may not go to this place of punishment.
verses.29: Abram says, “They have Moses and the prophets. They have listened to them.”
verses.30: And he said, “No, Father Abraham. But if anyone from the dead comes to them, then they may repent.”
verses.31: He said to him, “If Moises and the prophets are not obeyed, then no one will be able to be raised from the dead.”
